pack.risks: unvalidated idea; tiny DEMO risk only

concerns: Falsification criterion is decoupled from the hypothesis: exploration trades can be net-negative while cost calibration still succeeds, and vice versa, so 'negative costed expectancy' neither confirms nor refutes the >=20% misestimation claim.

affected_files mismatch: bot/aegis/research/promote.py is the claimed bias site but is not listed; bot/ai_council/ appears irrelevant; fill telemetry would naturally be emitted along the governed execution path (run_broker_paper.py chain), which is also unlisted.

~50 fills spread across multiple active symbols cannot support a per-symbol conclusion; spreads widen sharply around session opens and news, so unstratified sampling risks calibrating to an unrepresentative regime.
Measurement ambiguity: requested-vs-filled differs from mid-vs-filled, and MT5 commission and swap materially affect true round-trip cost; partial fills and volume weighting are unaddressed.
Logging must remain strictly observational: no mt5.order_send() calls from research components and zero added latency or gating interference in the order/confirmed-close path.
Raw fill logs must not overwrite or contaminate runtime intel artifacts consumed by champion promotion, and the experiment must be registered in ExperimentRegistry before the first measurement.
votes.reason: Calibrating the promote-gate cost model against measured MT5 DEMO fills is a legitimate, safety-compatible observational study: it places no new orders, involves no live exposure, leaves governed promotion untouched, and directly targets a plausible bias source (static spread/slippage assumptions distorting challenger-vs-champion EV in bot/aegis/research/promote.py). However, the specification has material gaps before testing: the falsification criterion (negative costed expectancy of exploration trades) does not test the stated >=20% cost-misestimation hypothesis; affected_files omit the very module named in the hypothesis while listing bot/ai_council/ which the design does not touch; ~50 total fills is statistically thin for a per-symbol claim given strong session-dependent spread variation; and the measurement definitions (price anchor, commission/swap treatment, round-trip formula) are unspecified. The idea is worth running once these are fixed.
requested_revisions: Rewrite falsification criteria to mirror the hypothesis, e.g.: reject calibration if no actively traded symbol shows a statistically significant >=20% deviation of realized round-trip cost from the static assumption, with predefined per-symbol minimum n and a stated estimator (bootstrap CI or median+MAD).
Correct affected_files to include bot/aegis/research/promote.py (cost-model consumer) and the actual execution-path module emitting fill telemetry; drop bot/ai_council/ unless genuinely modified.

Define the exact measurement schema: entry and exit slippage anchored to both requested price and prevailing mid at submission, explicit inclusion/exclusion of commission, swap, and volume-weighted partial fills, plus symbol, direction, volume, epoch timestamps, session bucket, and news-window flag per record.
Replace the flat ~50-order budget with per-symbol minimum sample counts and a session-stratified sampling plan, fixed before data collection begins.
Store raw fill records append-only under bot/research/ (not bot/intel/) and create the ExperimentRegistry entry before the first logged order.

Scope this proposal to measurement-only; any subsequent adoption of calibrated costs into promote.py must come back as a separate proposal including historical challengers re-scored under calibrated costs and a green pytest baseline.

concerns: The proposal does not specify that data collection is passive from existing authorized DEMO orders; trades must never be forced to reach 50 samples.

Realized cost definitions are incomplete: requested price, fill price, commissions, swaps, spread, partial fills, rejected orders, and confirmed-close prices require a consistent symbol-normalized methodology.
A 50-order sample may be insufficient across symbols, sessions, volatility regimes, and directions.
Promotion-gate calibration must remain an experiment/challenger input until sealed OOS validation and all existing promotion gates pass.
Affected files omit the governed execution owner/logging path needed to collect authoritative fill data.
votes.reason: Measured DEMO-fill costs can improve research realism, but the proposal lacks a governed measurement design and must not create or alter execution behavior to obtain samples.
requested_revisions: State explicitly that only bot/scripts/run_broker_paper.py may record broker execution data and that collection is passive from already-authorized MT5 DEMO trades.
Define the cost formula, units, handling of partial/rejected orders, commissions/swaps, close confirmation, and immutable provenance records.
Pre-register the experiment in ExperimentRegistry, define symbol/session stratification, minimum samples, and a held-out OOS comparison against the static model.
Keep calibrated costs isolated from champion promotion and live-facing artifacts until promote.py gates and sealed-holdout validation approve it.
Specify that DEMO-account, allow_live=false, mt5_demo mode, paper-trading, and existing risk/OMS/EV gates remain unchanged.

concerns: The sample size, symbols, measurement window, and statistical acceptance criteria are unspecified.
Realized spread/slippage definitions and requested-versus-filled price handling are not specified, including confirmed close prices and units.
The proposal does not explicitly state that only bot/scripts/run_broker_paper.py may submit MT5 orders and that all other research components remain read-only.
The claim of no champion impact needs enforcement details ensuring promote.py and champion artifacts cannot be modified by the experiment.
Logging order and fill data may create sensitive or incomplete records unless schema, persistence, and failure handling are defined.
votes.reason: The experiment is potentially useful and DEMO-only, but the proposal lacks sufficient operational and governance detail to approve testing. It must explicitly preserve the designated Firehose execution owner, DEMO safeguards, existing risk and promotion gates, and research-only restrictions.
requested_revisions: Specify symbols, execution horizon, target sample size, minimum data-quality requirements, and statistical method for estimating cost deviation.
Define entry and close realized-cost calculations, spread/slippage units, timestamps, partial fills, rejected orders, and missing confirmed-close handling.

State and test that execution remains exclusively through bot/scripts/run_broker_paper.py with mode mt5_demo, allow_live false, paper_trading_enabled true, DEMO-account verification, and existing risk gates unchanged.
Add explicit safeguards preventing changes to intelligent_champion.json or promotion decisions during the experiment.
Register the experiment in ExperimentRegistry and define an auditable report, rollback procedure, and falsification thresholds before collecting data.
